title: One convolutional layer
caption: Each output activation reads only a K-by-K window of the input, and the same W is used at every spatial position. Local connectivity shrinks the weight count per detector; sharing multiplies each weight's reuse by the number of positions. The two constraints are the whole CNN bias.

symbols.name: output activation
symbols.meaning: feature-map value at row i, column j, output channel k

symbols.name: input window
symbols.meaning: input pixel at offset (u,v) inside the kernel footprint, channel c

symbols.name: kernel weights
symbols.meaning: K x K x C_in x C_out parameters shared across all positions

symbols.name: bias
symbols.meaning: one scalar per output channel

symbols.name: input channel
symbols.meaning: sums over every input channel in the window

symbols.name: kernel offsets
symbols.meaning: positions inside the K x K stencil

symbols.name: activation
symbols.meaning: element-wise nonlinearity applied after the sum

title: Depthwise-separable cost ratio
caption: Splitting a K x K convolution into a per-channel spatial filter plus a 1 x 1 channel mix divides parameters and MACs by roughly the larger of C_out or K^2 - about 8-9x for 3 x 3 kernels. The saving is real arithmetic, but the depthwise stage has no cross-channel reuse, so its arithmetic intensity drops and wall-clock speedup lags the FLOP count on wide-GEMM hardware.

symbols.name: depthwise-separable cost
symbols.meaning: parameters or MACs of the two-stage factorization

symbols.name: standard conv cost
symbols.meaning: parameters or MACs of the monolithic K x K x C_in x C_out kernel

symbols.name: output channels
symbols.meaning: channel mix width; its inverse is the pointwise term

symbols.name: kernel area
symbols.meaning: spatial positions per filter; its inverse is the depthwise term

symbols.name: kernel side
symbols.meaning: spatial extent of each per-channel filter (3 for MobileNetV2)

title: Scaled dot-product attention
caption: Content-based routing: every query scores against every key, softmax turns scores into mixing weights, and the output is a weighted sum of values. The QK^T product is where the S-squared score work lives - the family's signature cost. Dividing by sqrt(d_k) keeps score magnitudes out of the softmax's saturated tail as head width grows.

symbols.name: queries
symbols.meaning: S x d_k projected representations, one row per position

symbols.name: keys
symbols.meaning: S x d_k projections each query is scored against

symbols.name: values
symbols.meaning: S x d_v content actually mixed by the weights

symbols.name: score matrix
symbols.meaning: S x S pairwise relevance scores; the quadratic term

symbols.name: scale factor
symbols.meaning: per-head dimension root; stops dot products saturating softmax

symbols.name: head dimension
symbols.meaning: feature width of each attention head (d_model / heads)

symbols.name: row normalizer
symbols.meaning: turns each row of scores into weights summing to 1

title: Where the quadratic term takes over
caption: Inside one transformer block the dense projections plus a 4x-width FFN cost 12·S·d^2 MACs while the two attention products cost 2·S^2·d. Setting them equal puts the crossover at six times the hidden width - about 9,600 tokens for a 1,600-wide model. Below it, ordinary GEMMs dominate; the quadratic is a long-context phenomenon.

symbols.name: sequence length
symbols.meaning: tokens processed together; batch folded into the per-request view

symbols.name: hidden width
symbols.meaning: model dimension d_model (1,600 for GPT-2 XL)

symbols.name: dense work
symbols.meaning: QKV + output projections (4Sd^2) plus FFN (8Sd^2) per block

symbols.name: attention work
symbols.meaning: score product QK^T (S^2d) plus the V mix (S^2d)

symbols.name: crossover
symbols.meaning: context length where attention arithmetic equals dense arithmetic

title: Decode arithmetic intensity
caption: Autoregressive decode at batch one is a GEMV: each FP16 weight is read once and participates in one MAC (2 FLOPs) per emitted token. The ratio never rises with better kernels - only batching or weight reuse lifts it. A 70B model therefore streams over 100 GB of weights per token, and the weight read alone costs about a millisecond at HBM speeds.

symbols.name: decode intensity
symbols.meaning: FLOPs per byte of weight traffic during token generation

symbols.name: MAC work
symbols.meaning: one multiply plus one add per weight per token

symbols.name: weight read
symbols.meaning: FP16 weight size; FP32 halves the ratio to 0.5

title: KV cache size per request
caption: Decode never recomputes past keys and values: each layer stores one K and one V per past token. GPT-2 XL (48 layers, width 1,600, FP16) burns about 307 KB per token, so the cache crosses the ~3 GB weight footprint near ten thousand tokens of context, then keeps growing linearly with context and concurrency.

symbols.name: cache bytes
symbols.meaning: resident memory one request's KV state occupies

symbols.name: layer count
symbols.meaning: transformer blocks each holding their own K/V (48 for GPT-2 XL)

symbols.name: K and V
symbols.meaning: two tensors per token per layer

symbols.name: model width
symbols.meaning: hidden dimension each stored vector spans

symbols.name: context length
symbols.meaning: past tokens retained; the linear-growth term

symbols.name: element size
symbols.meaning: 2 for FP16; quantization shrinks the cache linearly

title: Materialized score memory
caption: If the S x S score matrix is written out, storage grows quadratically: doubling context quadruples it, and 512 to 4096 tokens is a 64x blowup. Across all layers of a GPT-2 XL-shaped model, materialized scores would fill an 80 GB accelerator around 20-40K tokens - which is why tiled kernels stream the scores through registers instead of materializing them. The arithmetic stays quadratic; only the storage is optional.

symbols.name: score storage
symbols.meaning: bytes needed to hold all pairwise attention scores

symbols.name: score count
symbols.meaning: one score per query-key pair; the quadratic driver

symbols.name: element size
symbols.meaning: bytes per stored score (2 FP16, 4 FP32)

symbols.name: layer count
symbols.meaning: multiplies if every layer's scores are held at once

symbols.name: sequence length
symbols.meaning: positions scored against each other

title: Training state per parameter
caption: Holding a model for training costs four FP32-sized slots per parameter: weights, gradients, and Adam's two moments (momentum and variance). GPT-2 XL's ~24 GB of parameter state fits one accelerator; DLRM's embedding-heavy footprint does not - which is why table capacity, not compute, decides its cluster shape.

symbols.name: training state
symbols.meaning: persistent optimizer plus gradient memory for the whole model

symbols.name: parameter count
symbols.meaning: trainable weights; for DLRM the table rows dominate

symbols.name: bytes per param
symbols.meaning: 4B weights + 4B gradients + 8B Adam m and v
